PROTECTION ORDERS

By: Ntokozo Miya | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Victims in possession of protection orders continue to die at the hands of their abusers – we investigate why this document does not provide the protection it promises.

Unique Selling Point:
We speak to victims who share their difficulties in getting protection orders issued and enforced. We also map years of promises to give victims of gender-based violence access to the justice department services aimed at protecting them – the most basic of which is the protection order. Over and above this, we speak to a reformed abuser who explains why in some cases this document could lead to increased abuse and violence being unleashed on the victim.

Summary:
For many victims, the first line of defence against abuse and harassment is a protection order. Despite campaigns, initiatives, summits and countless budget allocations over the years, victims complain about delays in getting this documents. Many who do eventually get it say that it is not effectively enforced by police. The insert highlights the cracks in the system and interrogates why we are failing dismally to protect victims of GBV.

Further information:
Even the justice department acknowledges system barriers in protecting victims and the Deputy Minister has asked the Public Protector to investigate the complaints of victims and various rights groups. To remedy delays in getting an order of protection issued, the justice department plans to launch an online application process for the document. Regarding enforcement, the SAPS responds to tough questions about enforcement failures as well as apparent misunderstandings in the handling of protection orders. NGO's and activists pinpoint exactly where authorities are failing and give solution suggestions based on work they do on the ground.

Script:


PROTECTION ORDERS – POST-VIEWING FINAL

AUDIO
INTRO – UPSOUND - COMMENTATOR

It's over! It's Baby Lee at the Orient Theatre, punching the air in victory and in celebration! A star is born!
VO – Born in the Eastern Cape, the province fondly called the Mecca of boxing, Leighandre 'Baby Lee' Jegels was a talented fighter.

At twenty-five, she'd already punched her way to two major titles - the South African Junior Bantamweight and the Pan African Flyweight championships.

But there was one fight Leighandre would never win.
RITA JEGELS – LEIGHANDRE'S MOTHER

It wasn't a very good relationship. For about two years, they were together. We'd see her arms are blue. One time I saw her eye was blue, her neck, her back.
VO – In June last year, Leighandre broke up with her abusive boyfriend, Bulelani Manyakama, a police officer.
ANCEL JEGELS – LEIGHANDRE'S FATHER

He had said he was going to kill her and that's the reason why we took out the protection order.
VO – But the harassment did not stop.

A court issued a warrant for his arrest on the 1st of August but it was not executed.

On the 30th, at breakfast with friends, Leighandre smiled for the camera, not knowing that these would be her last photos. Three hours later when her mother drove her to the gym, an unfamiliar car blocked their way.
RITA JEGELS – LEIGHANDRE'S MOTHER

She said: “Mommy, it's him.” The first shot came in my eye. It went under my eye through my nose and out. Another gunshot came, that's when he struck me in my shoulder. Leighandre, opened the door immediately. She said, Mommy, I love you and she jumped out of the car and she ran. I knew that he got her. I heard three shots.
VO – Leighandre's protection order was folded neatly in her purse while she lay on the street, dying. Her father was on the scene shortly after the shooting.
ANCEL JEGELS – LEIGHANDRE'S FATHER

My wife was all bloodied up from the gunshot wounds. I asked her: “Where is Leighandre?” She said: “She's laying somewhere in the bush.”
VO - Her parents say she died because police didn't have the will to act against one of their own.
LINK - A protection order is meant to be the first line of defence for victims of gender-based violence but experts say that 5% of women killed by their partners were in possession of this document.




VO – A protection order instructs an offender to cease abusive behaviour. A victim applies for the order at a police station and then takes the application to court for consideration.

An interim order is issued with a date on which the accused must appear to argue why it should not be made final, explains Justice Department Deputy Minister John Jeffery.
JOHN JEFFERY – DEPUTY MINISTER, JUSTICE & CORRECTIONAL SERVICES DEPARTMENT

And then if the person breaks that order, then you can actually have them arrested and they can be criminally charged.
VO – Last year, more than one hundred and forty-five thousand applications were processed. Close to ninety-thousand interim orders were granted and over fifty thousand of those were made final.

Among the final orders, was Leighandre's.

Trained by former world champions, Zolani Tete and Vuyani Bhungu, Leighandre was a powerhouse, reminisces her promoter Andile Sidinile.
ANDILE SIDINILE – SIJUTA PROMOTIONS

There was a girl that we brought to fight her. We had to take this girl to the hospital because she had a fractured rib because of Leighandre's punches.
VO – But the hard-hitting champ was powerless in her relationship, even more so when her former lover got a protection order of his own.
ANCEL JEGELS – LEIGHANDRE'S FATHER

He weighed like, 110kg. How do you want to protect yourself from a 52kg child?
VO – Leighandre's parents say he used this document to intimidate her before he eventually killed her.
ANCEL JEGELS – LEIGHANDRE'S FATHER

25:22 - And not just one, three, four of them come here to serve her with a protection order from him because he's a police officer.
VO – Bulelani died from injuries he sustained in a car accident while fleeing from police hours after the shooting. The case was handed over to the Independent Police Investigative Directorate.

Chairperson of the South African Civil Society for Women's, Adolescents' and Children's Health, Precious Robinson, says many survivors complain that unless the order is served on the culprit and enforced effectively, it really is just a piece of paper.
PRECIOUS ROBINSON – SACSOWACH

Only 17 per cent of them actually were served, not even to be actioned, to be served to say: 'Look, sir, you are not supposed to be doing 1, 2, 3, 4.
VO – This Sowetan mother of two says back in 2017, police told her that she would have to deliver the order to the man who was harassing her.

He was romantically interested in her and would not take no for an answer.
ABUSE VICTIM

They refused to help me because he's a CPF member of that police station I went to.
VO – Though the order was not officially served, he knew it had been issued. His verbal assaults and intimidation escalated to outright sexual harassment.
ABUSE VICTIM

Always, he passed where I stay and do some silly things, touching me, my body, my private parts.
VO – His ties with the local police meant no one dared to intervene on her behalf.

A protection order does not expire and for two years, she struggled to have it enforced. The final straw came early this year when her abuser took out an order against her.
ABUSE VICTIM

I've decided to take my children and go and stay somewhere else because I never got help from the police.
VO – Since she moved, she hasn't seen her tormentor.

Actor Patrick Shai is a reformed abuser and founder of Khuluma Ndoda, a wellness group for men. His turning point came after filming a scene in which he played an aggressive husband and father.
PATRICK SHAI – KHULUMA NDODA

I saw the horror that I was bringing into the hearts and minds of people that I professed to love for the first time.
VO - He says violence is likely to escalate after a protection order is issued.
PATRICK SHAI – KHULUMA NDODA

The abuser feels like you are undermining their power and they want to affirm themselves by becoming even more violent and even more abusive. Just to say, to show you that this piece of paper means nothing.
VO – He says further victimisation is the reason many people withdraw protection orders.
LINK - After years of protests by civil society demanding decisive action against gender-based violence, authorities are exploring new ways to make protection orders work better for victims.
VO - Government spends millions on programs meant to provide a lifeline for abused people but the problem persists.
CLAIRE - CB – Where should we be spending that money? What are we doing wrong?
PRECIOUS ROBINSON – SACSOWACH

Let us have a system that connects us to where this national command or gender based violence thing is so that this can be prevented, deaths can be prevented.
VO – A centralised database that can be accessed and actioned by all stakeholders means victims can avoid police stations and courts where some abusers have connections.
JOHN JEFFERY – DEPUTY MINISTER, JUSTICE & CORRECTIONAL SERVICES DEPARTMENT

That has been a gap which we are aiming to correct with the Domestic Violence Amendment Act, amendment bill.
VO – The department hopes the bill will be introduced next month.


JOHN JEFFERY – DEPUTY MINISTER, JUSTICE & CORRECTIONAL SERVICES DEPARTMENT

Part of that provides that you can do online orders. Generally if you go there in the morning, the order should be granted on the same day. Once you've got the order, it has to be served on the person you've got it against. The amendments also allow for electronic service on them.
VO – Kerryn Rehse of MOSAIC, a social justice advocacy group, says their SAFE project promotes a coordinated response to protection order violations.
KERRYN REHSE – MOSAIC

The SAFE platform really acts to procreate safe plans and coordinate collective efforts to respond and prevent domestic violence. The important part for us, the pure accountability mechanism, where different stakeholders are able to hold each other accountable for their agreed response as well as prevention efforts.
VO – The project was set in motion at Western Cape's Philippi police station where MOSAIC counsels survivors of abuse.

In this financial year, the police ministry set aside fifty million rands for resources and personnel to strengthen the response to violence and abuse.

Brigadier Vishnu Naidoo says all officers are trained on gender-based violence matters.
BRIG. VISHNU NAIDOO – SAPS – ACR PHONE CALL RECORDING

They trained on legislation, policies, directives, social context, attending to violence assistance of victims of domestic violence.
VO – No victim must be turned away.
BRIG. VISHNU NAIDOO – SAPS – ACR PHONE CALL RECORDING

We deal very decisively with members that do that. Members are dismissed. Members are charged.
VO – As for protection orders being used as a tool to further harass victims...
BRIG. VISHNU NAIDOO – SAPS – ACR PHONE CALL RECORDING

We have to respond equally to every case. There shouldn't be preference given to any case.
LINK - While authorities scramble for solutions, a grieving father is overcome by guilt because he was not there to protect his daughter.
VO - On the day that Leighandre was killed, her father attended to a work emergency – it was the first time in weeks that he had not accompanied his wife and daughter.
ANCEL JEGELS – LEIGHANDRE'S FATHER

If I didn't do that, he wouldn't have done this here. Because he was a coward, man. He was really a coward. He never ever came close to Leighandre when I was with her.










PROMOS

Victims say even after getting protection orders, the system failed them and left them vulnerable to further abuse – we investigate why this document doesn't always deliver on its promise of protection.

A protection order is meant to shield victims of domestic violence and sexual harassment but they say, the piece of paper means nothing if authorities do not enforce it decisively.

We investigate why a protection order, a document intended to protect victims of abuse and harassment from further violence and torment, isn't much of a deterrent to offenders.

ABUSE VICTIM I've decided to take my children and go and stay somewhere else because I never got help from the police. VO – Since she moved, she hasn't seen her tormentor. Actor Patrick Shai is a reformed abuser and founder of Khuluma Ndoda, a wellness group for men. His turning point came after filming a scene in which he played an aggressive husband and father. PATRICK SHAI – KHULUMA NDODA I saw the horror that I was bringing into the hearts and minds of people that I professed to love for the first time. VO - He says violence is likely to escalate after a protection order is issued. PATRICK SHAI – KHULUMA NDODA The abuser feels like you are undermining their power and they want to affirm themselves by becoming even more violent and even more abusive. Just to say, to show you that this piece of paper means nothing. VO – He says further victimisation is the reason many people withdraw protection orders. LINK - After years of protests by civil society demanding decisive action against gender-based violence, authorities are exploring new ways to make protection orders work better for victims. VO - Government spends millions on programs meant to provide a lifeline for abused people but the problem persists. CLAIRE - CB – Where should we be spending that money? What are we doing wrong? PRECIOUS ROBINSON – SACSOWACH Let us have a system that connects us to where this national command or gender based violence thing is so that this can be prevented, deaths can be prevented. VO – A centralised database that can be accessed and actioned by all stakeholders means victims can avoid police stations and courts where some abusers have connections. JOHN JEFFERY – DEPUTY MINISTER, JUSTICE & CORRECTIONAL SERVICES DEPARTMENT That has been a gap which we are aiming to correct with the Domestic Violence Amendment Act, amendment bill. VO – The department hopes the bill will be introduced next month. JOHN JEFFERY – DEPUTY MINISTER, JUSTICE & CORRECTIONAL SERVICES DEPARTMENT Part of that provides that you can do online orders. Generally if you go there in the morning, the order should be granted on the same day. Once you've got the order, it has to be served on the person you've got it against. The amendments also allow for electronic service on them. VO – Kerryn Rehse of MOSAIC, a social justice advocacy group, says their SAFE project promotes a coordinated response to protection order violations. KERRYN REHSE – MOSAIC The SAFE platform really acts to procreate safe plans and coordinate collective efforts to respond and prevent domestic violence. The important part for us, the pure accountability mechanism, where different stakeholders are able to hold each other accountable for their agreed response as well as prevention efforts. VO – The project was set in motion at Western Cape's Philippi police station where MOSAIC counsels survivors of abuse. In this financial year, the police ministry set aside fifty million rands for resources and personnel to strengthen the response to violence and abuse. Brigadier Vishnu Naidoo says all officers are trained on gender-based violence matters. BRIG. VISHNU NAIDOO – SAPS – ACR PHONE CALL RECORDING They trained on legislation, policies, directives, social context, attending to violence assistance of victims of domestic violence. VO – No victim must be turned away. BRIG. VISHNU NAIDOO – SAPS – ACR PHONE CALL RECORDING We deal very decisively with members that do that. Members are dismissed. Members are charged. VO – As for protection orders being used as a tool to further harass victims... BRIG. VISHNU NAIDOO – SAPS – ACR PHONE CALL RECORDING We have to respond equally to every case. There shouldn't be preference given to any case. LINK - While authorities scramble for solutions, a grieving father is overcome by guilt because he was not there to protect his daughter. VO - On the day that Leighandre was killed, her father attended to a work emergency – it was the first time in weeks that he had not accompanied his wife and daughter. ANCEL JEGELS – LEIGHANDRE'S FATHER If I didn't do that, he wouldn't have done this here. Because he was a coward, man. He was really a coward. He never ever came close to Leighandre when I was with her. PROMOS Victims say even after getting protection orders, the system failed them and left them vulnerable to further abuse – we investigate why this document doesn't always deliver on its promise of protection. A protection order is meant to shield victims of domestic violence and sexual harassment but they say, the piece of paper means nothing if authorities do not enforce it decisively. We investigate why a protection order, a document intended to protect victims of abuse and harassment from further violence and torment, isn't much of a deterrent to offenders.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Victims in possession of protection orders continue to die at the hands of their abusers – we investigate why this document does not provide the protection it promises.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We speak to victims who share their difficulties in getting protection orders issued and enforced. We also map years of promises to give victims of gender-based violence access to the justice department services aimed at protecting them – the most basic of which is the protection order. Over and above this, we speak to a reformed abuser who explains why in some cases this document could lead to increased abuse and violence being unleashed on the victim.
metadata.Summary: For many victims, the first line of defence against abuse and harassment is a protection order. Despite campaigns, initiatives, summits and countless budget allocations over the years, victims complain about delays in getting this documents. Many who do eventually get it say that it is not effectively enforced by police. The insert highlights the cracks in the system and interrogates why we are failing dismally to protect victims of GBV.
metadata.Further information: Even the justice department acknowledges system barriers in protecting victims and the Deputy Minister has asked the Public Protector to investigate the complaints of victims and various rights groups. To remedy delays in getting an order of protection issued, the justice department plans to launch an online application process for the document. Regarding enforcement, the SAPS responds to tough questions about enforcement failures as well as apparent misunderstandings in the handling of protection orders. NGO's and activists pinpoint exactly where authorities are failing and give solution suggestions based on work they do on the ground.
